div.head: ADVERTISEMENT.
div.p:
The following Discourses were composed in the autumn of 1818, and delivered as a regular series of afternoon Lectures in the Chapel of the British Minister at Berlin. Though designed for a particular place and auditory, they may be found not inapplicable to others. The author submits them to the public, with all the apprehensions of an author, yet not without an humble hope that they may be useful to some of his Reverend brethren, especially to such as have lately entered on the Holy Office. Few Ministers can be long engaged in the duties of the pulpit, particularly in the remoter parts of the kingdom, without discovering that a large majority of their congregation stands full as much in need of instruction in the elementary and historical parts of Scripture, as in the higher doctrines of revelation; and that a total ignorance of the
former, renders any progress in the latter tedious and uncertain.

In the construction of these Lectures, the author has by no means relied on his own resources, nor rejected the valuable aid of those who have preceded him in knowledge as well as time. He regrets that such aid was in the present instance attainable by memory rather than reference. But the fact is, that his whole professional library, during his residence at Berlin, did not contain a dozen volume, including the Bible.

His readers, no doubt, will readily discover the track of his studies; and that they may not think him desirous of concealing, or capable of denying his obligations to abler writers tahn himself, he takes this opportunity of avowing, that they are very considerable to Dr. Olinthius Gregory, in whose Letters he has found a never-failing treasure of knowledge, argument, and eloquence, and to whom, though perfectly unknown, he is most happy in paying this tribute of gratitude and respect.
